name: Badge
summary: A small status indicator overlaid on the corner of an icon or navigation item, showing that something changed without interrupting the user. Use a dot for a plain attention signal, a numeral for a short count or label.

inputs.name: anchor
inputs.description: The icon or item the badge is positioned against. The badge itself contributes no size to the layout; it overlays the anchor's top-trailing corner.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Short text or number shown inside the container. Its presence, not a separate flag, switches the badge from a small dot to a larger numeral/label container.

inputs.name: containerColor
inputs.description: Overrides the badge container colour (comp.badge.color or comp.badge.large-color, chosen by whether label is present).

anatomy.name: Anchor
anatomy.description: The icon or navigation item the badge is attached to. Not part of the badge itself, but drives its offset.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The coloured shape: a small dot with no label, or a larger pill/circle when it carries content.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Short text or number inside the container. Only present on the numeral variant.

variants.description: No label content: a presence/attention signal with no information, sized and shaped by comp.badge.size/shape/color.

Carries a short count or label, sized and shaped by comp.badge.large-size/large-shape/large-color/large-label-text-*. Rendered whenever label content is supplied — it is the same composable with an optional slot, not a separate one (Badge.kt:155-162).

layout.text: The container's size token is a minimum, not a fixed size: a numeral badge widens automatically to fit its label rather than clipping.
When the label needs more horizontal room than a circle (e.g. two or more digits), the container gets 4dp of extra padding on each side of the text, which is what turns the circle into a pill.
Anchor offset is hard-coded in dp, not token-driven, and differs by variant: a dot badge is pulled 6dp in from the anchor's trailing edge and 6dp down from its top edge.

A numeral badge is pulled 12dp in horizontally and 14dp down vertically from the anchor's top-trailing corner — a deliberately larger overlap than the dot, to center the numeral over the corner rather than hang off it.
Both offsets are measured from the anchor's top-trailing corner independent of the anchor's own size — a 24dp icon and a 40dp touch target get the same offset.

No digit-count truncation logic exists in Badge.kt; label content is exactly whatever the caller passes. A kit implementation must own overflow formatting (e.g. "999+") explicitly rather than assume the renderer provides it.

behaviour.text: Badge has no interaction states of its own (no hover, press or focus); it is not touchable, and taps on its area land on the anchor beneath it.

There is no built-in appear/disappear or content-change animation — Badge.kt has no transition, AnimatedVisibility or animateContentSize. Any enter/exit or dot-to-numeral size morph must be built at the call site.

semantics: The badge itself carries no independent touch target or role; it is a presentation-only overlay.
Accessibility semantics (e.g. "3 unread") belong on the anchor's own content description, not on the badge, since there is no dedicated announcement for a badge appearing or its count changing.

notes.text: Model badge as one composable with an optional label slot that switches its size/shape/colour token group, not as two hard variants selected by a flag — this keeps a dot-to-numeral transition a content-driven resize rather than a variant switch.
The dot offset (6dp/6dp) and the numeral offset (12dp/14dp) are deliberately different constants, not a shared value — keep two offset pairs rather than collapsing them into one "badge offset".

The "999+" overflow convention is not in Badge.kt; it is carried over conceptually from the View-system BadgeDrawable's maxCharacterCount/maxNumber attributes in MDC-Android. Treat digit-cap formatting as a decision the kit must document explicitly.
